question: Ethanol on heating at 443 K in excess concentrated sulphuric acid gives ethene. The chemical change taking place is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**dehydration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ethanol (C₂H₅OH)** undergoes a chemical reaction in the presence of **concentrated sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄)** when heated at **443 K**.
 
• This reaction leads to the removal of a **water molecule (H₂O)** from ethanol, producing **ethene (C₂H₄)**. This process is called **dehydration**__.
 
• **Concentrated sulphuric acid** acts as a **dehydrating agent** in this reaction, facilitating the removal of water.
 
• The chemical equation for the reaction is:

 C₂H₅OH → C₂H₄ + H₂O
 
• This reaction is an example of an **elimination reaction**, where a single compound splits into two products.
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is __**dehydration**__.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dehydration Reaction:**

 
 
• A **dehydration reaction** involves the removal of a water molecule from a compound.
 
• It is a common reaction in organic chemistry, especially in the conversion of alcohols to alkenes.
 
• **Example:** Ethanol to ethene is a classic example of a dehydration reaction.
 
 
 
• **Role of Sulphuric Acid:**
 
 
• Concentrated sulphuric acid acts as a **dehydrating agent** by absorbing water formed during the reaction.
 
• It also acts as a **catalyst** to facilitate the reaction.
 
 
 
• **Ethene:**
 
 
• **Ethene (C₂H₄)** is an alkene and the simplest member of the alkene family.
 
• It is a colorless gas with a slightly sweet odor and is widely used in the production of plastics like polyethylene.
 
 
 
• **Other Reaction Types:**
 
 
• **Oxidation:** Involves the addition of oxygen or removal of hydrogen. Ethanol, when oxidized, forms acetic acid, not ethene.
 
• **Reduction:** Involves the removal of oxygen or the addition of hydrogen. This is not applicable in this context.
 
• **Halogenation:** Involves the addition of halogen atoms (e.g., Cl, Br). This does not occur in this reaction.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The reaction is temperature-sensitive. Heating ethanol to **443 K** is essential to initiate the dehydration process.
 
• **Concentrated sulphuric acid** must be used in excess to ensure complete dehydration.
 
• The reaction pathway involves the formation of a **carbocation intermediate**, which then eliminates water to form ethene.
 
• Dehydration reactions are widely used in industrial processes to produce alkenes, which are essential in the production of polymers and other chemicals.
